decisions.question: How many tasks, and where do their boundaries fall, under constraint 1 (every task but the last starts with a failing test) and constraint 3 (at most 5)?

options.label: 3 tasks: Mermaid with the shared helpers; Graphviz; gate and doc
options.consequence: each code task has a real red step (8 tests failing with UnimplementedError) and a reviewer can reject one renderer while approving the other; the shared helpers land with their first user, so nothing private is unused at Task 1 (no unused_element warning)

options.label: 4 tasks: shared helpers alone first, then Mermaid, then Graphviz, then the doc
options.consequence: the helpers are private and testable only through a renderer, so a helpers task has no failing test of its own and breaks constraint 1, or needs a src-public seam only for tests

options.label: 4 or 5 tasks: a separate task for the corner-case tests
options.consequence: those tests pass against Tasks 1 and 2's code, so the task has no failing first step and breaks constraint 1

decisions.chosen: 3 tasks: Mermaid with the shared helpers; Graphviz; gate and doc
decisions.why: The only split a reviewer can meaningfully reject one side of is the renderer split; per-rule tests belong in the task whose code they pin. The dry run shows both code tasks red then green (T1.2 to T1.4: 353 to 361; T2.2 to T2.4: 361 to 369), and the G22 cases turning green only in Task 2, because both remaining cases call both renderers.

decisions.question: One library with private helpers, or a second library under lib/src/render/ for the shared label, duration and arrow helpers?

options.label: one library, private helpers
options.consequence: renderers.dart grows from 15 to 187 lines; no src-public names; matches nidana.model.13's codec precedent and the phase estimate of about 3 files

options.label: renderers.dart plus labels.dart
options.consequence: the helpers become src-public and directly testable, at the cost of a second set of names no other library uses

decisions.why: The helpers are one rule set that only the two renderers apply; D4 names the directory, not the file count, and the codec phase chose the same. The renderers' tests pin every helper through the rendered text.

decisions.question: How are labels built and escaped: per line then joined, or the joined label escaped once?

options.label: lists of unescaped lines, each escaped, then joined by the renderer's break
options.consequence: follows the rule text literally ('Labels are lines of text, each escaped, then joined'); one label function per part shared by both renderers

options.label: build the joined label, then escape it
options.consequence:
escapes Mermaid's
into #lt;br/#gt; and doubles Graphviz's \n break; the dry run's D3 fails the gate

decisions.chosen: lists of unescaped lines, each escaped, then joined by the renderer's break
decisions.why: It is what the contract says, and the seeded D3 shows the other reading breaks every golden. Escapes run in the rule's order (Mermaid's '#' first, Graphviz's backslash first; D1 and D2 fail the gate otherwise) and touch nothing else (D4 and D5).

decisions.question: What does an anonymous retry render as? No render/ golden holds one (S148).

options.label: retry (anonymous)
options.consequence: applies 'An anonymous reference renders as (anonymous)' to every function reference, as the samples already do for an anonymous transformer

options.label: retry alone
options.consequence: reads 'the retry's name when it has one' as 'when the retry has a name'; an anonymous transformer would then by parallel reading drop its line, which the escaping golden contradicts (filter then (anonymous))

options.label: no retry line
options.consequence: hides that the edge retries at all, which the IR records

decisions.why: The contract settles it: the sentence about anonymous references is general, and the transformer clause has the same 'when it has one' shape while the goldens render an anonymous transformer as (anonymous). Not a rule gap; the missing golden is a coverage gap, reported in contract_gaps. Signal that would change this: an hsdd-contract ruling that 'it' means the reference.
evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/renderers-plan/output.txt D6 (passes the gate, fails both package tests)

decisions.question: How does the arrow walk find a topic's node id, and how do the two renderers share the walk?

options.label: one walk returning records, ids from a Map keyed by the whole TopicRef
options.consequence: each renderer only formats ({from, to, dedup}); one name of two variants keeps two ids; lookups are O(1)

options.label: graph.topics.indexOf per lookup, walk duplicated per renderer
options.consequence: same output, quadratic lookups and two copies of the order rule to keep in step

decisions.chosen: one walk returning records, ids from a Map keyed by the whole TopicRef
decisions.why: The order of arrows is the rule most likely to drift between two copies; one walk keeps it in one place. TopicRef equality is all three fields (topic-model@v1 G8), so the Map gives the rule's 't{i} of graph.topics'; the seeded D13 (keyed by name) passes the gate and fails the package tests.

decisions.question: Where do the package tests get the seven sample graphs for their own golden comparison?

options.label: decode valid/{name}.json with nidana.model.13's decoder
options.consequence: no dependency on the conformance library; relies on G20 (the decoder gives the sample back), which the gate already replays

options.label: import the conformance library by relative path for topologyIrSamples
options.consequence: imports package:nidana_contract_check/fixture.dart and package:matcher, neither a dependency of nidana_dart_contracts (ADR-002 item 3), so depend_on_referenced_packages would report it

options.label: re-declare the samples in test code
options.consequence: hundreds of lines copied from a fixture, drifting silently from it

decisions.why: It reaches the same graphs with the package's own public API and helpers that json_support.dart already has (fixtureJson, fixtureNames). The suite's own G22 case still compares the recorded samples.

decisions.question: How do the corner-case tests state what they expect?

options.label: the whole rendered text of a graph built for each rule, as a raw string
options.consequence: each test reads like a golden and pins ids, order, labels, escapes, indentation and newlines at once; 16 tests in two files of about 200 lines each

options.label: contains() checks of single lines
options.consequence: shorter, but misses order, duplicates and indentation, which are exactly what the goldens leave open (D12, D14)

decisions.chosen: the whole rendered text of a graph built for each rule, as a raw string
decisions.why: The rules not shown by any sample are mostly about order and repetition, which line checks cannot see. Only the duration table uses contains(), one line per duration, because its graph is otherwise fixed. The expected texts were written by hand from the rules and the dry run passed them on the first run.
evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/renderers-plan/output.txt D (every seeded defect fails at least one package test)

decisions.question: topology_graph_test.dart's header comment (lines 7 and 8) says the G22 render case waits for nidana.model.14's Mermaid renderer; edit it in this phase?

options.label: leave it; edit no existing test
options.consequence: the comment reads as history after this phase; the file set stays four new or changed files, as the precedent kept it

options.label: edit the comment in Task 2
options.consequence: one more file in the product diff for a comment, and an exception to 'edits no existing test'

decisions.why: It is a comment, not a pin, and describes what was true when nidana.model.11 wrote it. Low stakes either way; the orchestrator can fold a one-line comment fix into any later commit.

options.label: skip: the npm packages are not in the local cache

contract_gaps.where: hsdd/contract/fixture/topology-ir/render/ (G22 first clause) and hsdd/contract/topology-ir.md line 273
contract_gaps.problem: Low, non-blocking, coverage only. No render/ golden holds an anonymous retry, a duration above a second that is not whole seconds, a repeated input (one handle twice into combine or merge), one topic name of two variants, or a character the rules leave as it is beyond '$' and the backslash in Mermaid ('&', '|', '[', ']', a single quote). A renderer that writes 'retry null', rounds 1500ms to 1s, collapses repeated arrows, gives two variants of one name one id, or escapes '&' passes every replay of this node, nidana.model.14's unrestricted one included (S149 dry run, seeded D4, D6, D7, D12, D13). The rule text settles each case; for the anonymous retry, 'the retry's name when it has one' can be misread as 'when the retry has a name', which only the general sentence on anonymous references resolves.
contract_gaps.proposed_fix: hsdd-contract adds to an existing sample, or adds an eighth sample with its valid/ document and two render/ goldens, holding a switchMap with an anonymous retry, a duration of 1500ms or 1s and 1us, combine2 of one handle twice, two topics of one name and different variants, and a label with & | [ ] and a single quote; and rewords the edge bullet to 'retry and the retry's name, (anonymous) for an anonymous one, when the edge has a retry'. Compatible within v1 (no rule changes). This phase's package tests pin all five meanwhile.
